## Batch 7, January 2025

2.4 kg white cabbage from the veg stall at Levenshulme market, £1.80 for two heads. Outer leaves off and kept, cored, sliced 2 mm on the Benriner mandoline. Salt at 2% of the trimmed weight: 48 g fine sea salt, no iodine. 1.5 tsp caraway, 6 juniper berries crushed. Massaged with clean hands for 10 min until it's limp and sitting in its own brine.

## Packing

3 L Kilner jar, packed down hard in layers with the end of a rolling pin. Brine has to sit 2 cm over the top. Outer leaf tucked over as a cap, then a glass weight on that, see [[Fermentation weights and airlocks]]. Leave 4 cm headspace or it overflows in week one. Jar on a tray, because it will.

## Timeline

- room: 18°C in the commissary storeroom, Openshaw
- day 3: bubbling, brine level up
- day 7: tangy, still crunchy, already decent on a hot dog
- day 21: pH 3.4 on the Apera PH60, properly sharp. Into 500 ml jars, fridge
- yield 2.1 kg, about 13p per 100 g

## Kraut vs kimchi

Kraut is dry-salted at 2% and left alone. Kimchi gets a salt brine soak first, then a paste, and goes much faster, numbers are in [[Kimchi batch log]]. On the menu the kraut is KR-07, goes on the Reuben and the bratwurst roll.

## Notes from 7 batches

- 1.5% salt: went soft and slimy by day 10 (batch 3)
- 2.5%: too salty for the Reuben, had to rinse it
- kahm yeast on batch 5, white wrinkly film. Scraped off, kraut underneath fine. Harmless but ugly.
- red cabbage version (batch 6) with 1 grated apple: turns the brine purple, sells better at Christmas
- Rob says it sorts his stomach out, wrote it up in [[Fiber and gut health]]
